aboutGame.title: What is Backrooms?
paragraphs: Backrooms is a collaborative internet horror setting built on one idea: reality has a flaw, and slipping through it drops you into a dimension of endless, badly lit liminal spaces. It began as an anonymous 2019 post on 4chan's paranormal board, paired with a photo of an empty yellow room, and grew into wikis, video games, YouTube series, and a Hollywood film.

Today Backrooms spans dozens of interpretations. Escape the Backrooms sends up to four players through more than thirty levels, The Backrooms delivers a solo survival run, and the A24 feature film directed by Kane Parsons brought the mythos to cinemas in 2026. Our wiki gathers level walkthroughs, entity profiles, survival tactics, and lore in one place.

modules.name: Backrooms Game Guide
modules.description: A beginner-friendly overview of how to start playing Backrooms games, what the objective is, and the survival rules that apply before you explore deeper.

highlights.detail: Understand the premise: you no-clip out of reality into an endless maze of yellow rooms, damp carpet, and buzzing fluorescent lights.
Pick a version to play, from co-op titles like Escape the Backrooms to solo horror, free browser games, and Roblox experiences.
Learn the core loop: there is no map and no objective marker, so navigation and sound awareness are the real mechanics.
Treat entities as hazards rather than enemies, because you cannot fight them, only avoid, hide, and break line of sight.
Find the exit: every level has entrances and exits, and documenting them is how the community maps the Backrooms.

modules.name: Backrooms Levels Guide
modules.description: How the numbered Backrooms levels connect, which environments are safe, and how to read a level entry before you step through an exit.

highlights.label: Level 0
highlights.detail: The Lobby: mono-yellow rooms, damp carpet, buzzing lights, and the classic starting point for most wanderers.

highlights.label: Level 1
highlights.detail: The Habitable Zone: concrete halls, wooden crates, Almond Water, and the first real outposts.

highlights.label: Level 2
highlights.detail: Pipe Dreams: narrow industrial corridors, extreme heat, and poor visibility that punishes loud movement.

highlights.label: Poolrooms
highlights.detail: Level 37: interconnected tiled rooms and warm shallow water with almost no documented entities.

highlights.label: Negative
highlights.detail: Levels below zero where dream logic replaces geometry and navigation stops being reliable.

highlights.label: Level 94
highlights.detail: Motion: a grainy suburban town with a floating castle that looks calm but hides unstable physics.

modules.name: Backrooms Entities Guide
modules.description: The most documented Backrooms entities ranked by threat, from sapient wanderers you can trade with to predators that hunt by sound.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: Skin-Stealer (Entity 10) and Partygoer (Entity 67): mimics and lures that turn other survivors into bait.

highlights.label: A
highlights.detail: Smiler (Entity 3) and Hound (Entity 8): dark-corner ambushers and fast pack hunters on industrial levels.

highlights.label: B
highlights.detail: Deathmoth (Entity 4) and Faceling (Entity 9): territorial swarms and unpredictable humanoids you can usually avoid.

highlights.label: C
highlights.detail: Entity 1, the Humans, and Jerry: sapient groups you can talk and trade with, though never fully trust.

modules.name: Backrooms Survival Tips
modules.description: Practical Backrooms survival rules covering noise, stamina, sanity, and the habits that keep experienced wanderers alive.

highlights.label: Walk Quiet
highlights.detail: Sprinting through carpeted halls rings a dinner bell for entities; walk unless something is already chasing you.

highlights.label: Stamina
highlights.detail: Treat stamina as currency and never spend it all exploring a room you have already cleared.

highlights.label: Almond
highlights.detail: Carry Almond Water to steady your mind and slow the sanity drain of long solo runs.

highlights.label: Mark Walls
highlights.detail: Without a reliable map, count doors and mark junctions so you can retrace your route back to an exit.

highlights.label: Sightlines
highlights.detail: Use corners and doorways to break line of sight instead of running in a straight line from a pursuer.

highlights.label: Stay Calm
highlights.detail: The first minutes of quiet are the trap, and panic decisions cost more runs than any single entity.

modules.name: Backrooms Multiplayer Guide
modules.description: How co-op Backrooms games work, from proximity voice chat and squad roles to the team habits that stop a run from falling apart.

highlights.detail: Pick a co-op title: Backrooms: Escape Together supports up to five friends, while Escape the Backrooms runs up to four.
Set up voice early, because proximity chat is part of the tension and callouts matter once the squad splits up.
Assign roles: one player navigates and marks the route, another watches the rear, and the rest handle resources.
Decide when to split, since spreading out covers ground faster but entity-heavy levels punish anyone caught alone.
Regroup at every exit and never enter a new level until the whole squad is accounted for.

modules.name: Backrooms Lore Guide
modules.description: The story behind the Backrooms, from the original 2019 post and the M.E.G. to Async, the Complex, and the A24 film.

highlights.label: 2019 Post
highlights.detail: A single anonymous 4chan post and a yellow-room photo introduced no-clipping and the whole setting.

highlights.label: The Photo
highlights.detail: Researchers traced the original image to a 2002 furniture store renovation in Oshkosh, Wisconsin.

highlights.label: M.E.G.
highlights.detail: The Major Explorer Group is the largest explorer faction in fan lore, running outposts on habitable levels.

highlights.label: Async
highlights.detail: The research foundation in Kane Parsons' found-footage series studies the Backrooms and its Threshold experiments.

highlights.label: Complex
highlights.detail: Async's internal name for the Backrooms, tied to a 1982 magnetic distortion prototype and hidden portals.

highlights.label: A24 Film
highlights.detail: Kane Parsons directed the 2026 A24 adaptation, which follows a therapist searching for a missing patient.

modules.name: Backrooms Game Updates

highlights.detail: The original 4chan post introduces the yellow room and the idea of no-clipping out of reality.

faq.title: Backrooms FAQ
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about the Backrooms, its levels, entities, games, and lore.

items.question: What is the Backrooms?
items.answer: The Backrooms is a collaborative internet horror setting about an endless dimension of liminal spaces you reach by no-clipping out of reality. It began as an anonymous 2019 post and has grown into wikis, video games, and an A24 film.

items.question: How do you enter the Backrooms?
items.answer: In the lore you enter the Backrooms by no-clipping, a term borrowed from video game glitches where a character slips through the geometry of a level. There is no door, only a flaw in reality.

items.question: What is the most dangerous Backrooms entity?
items.answer: The Skin-Stealer (Entity 10) is the most dangerous Backrooms entity, mimicking voices and appearances to lure wanderers. The Smiler and the Hound are close behind on dark and industrial levels.

items.question: Is the Backrooms a real game?
items.answer: There is no single official Backrooms game. The setting has inspired many titles, including the co-op Escape the Backrooms, the solo horror game The Backrooms, mobile stealth entries, VR versions, and free Roblox experiences.

items.question: Where should beginners start in the Backrooms?
items.answer: Start with Level 0, the yellow halls, and learn to walk quietly, manage stamina, and find an exit before you explore deeper levels. Our Backrooms beginner and level guides cover each step.
